<b><i><p align="center">Unlock your Android phone with an alternative PIN - and trigger anything from a notification to a wipe. (Xposed, Root)</p></i></b>
</p>

This app provides a reliable way to run commands when entering a specific, wrong PIN on your Android lock screen.

Unlike [Duress](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=me.lucky.duress&hl=en&gl=US), this app uses Xposed Framework so you can also **unlock** your phone with an *alternative* PIN, preventing some *social engineering vulnerabilities*😇 And by the way, it also works before your first unlock after a reboot.

## Features

- Alternative PIN to unlock phone
- Run commands on alternative PIN with root (also supports pam_exec style to control unlock with your script!)
- Easy to use user interface
- Material You design

Currently tested on:
- Android 11-17 (LineageOS, x86_64 and arm64)
- Xiaomi HyperOS 3.0.8.0

Currently NOT working on:
- Android <= 10
- Samsung OneUI (WIP)
- OnePlus OxygenOS
- Tecno HiOS
- most other non-AOSP

It *should* also work on other architectures and devices if the system isn't cooked too much.

## How to Use

- Install Magisk / APatch / KernelSU or other root solutions, enable Zygisk (like [NeoZygisk](https://github.com/JingMatrix/NeoZygisk))
- Install LSPosed / Vector / Your favorite Xposed framework
- Install this module
- Activate this module in LSPosed settings (automatically enabled for SystemUI)
- Launch AlternativeUnlockXposed, grant superuser access, set your real password and alternative password
- (Optional) Set up what to do when entering the alternative PIN: change action to sudo, and set your command.
  - With "PAM style unlock" enabled, the command receives the entered credential via the `$AU_INPUT` environment variable, and its exit code decides whether the phone unlocks (0 = unlock, anything else = don't). See Examples below.
  - <details><summary>Examples:</summary>

    **1. Send a notification to your Telegram/Discord/Webhook:**

    ```bash
    curl "https://api.telegram.org/bot<your_token>/sendMessage" --json '{"chat_id": <your_user_id>, "text": "Phone unlocked with '$AU_INPUT'"}' & true;
    ```

    **2. Hide and disable apps:**

    ```bash
    for i in `pm list packages | grep -i -E 'telegram|sagernet|twitter|discord|tinder' | cut -d : -f 2` ; do pm disable $i; done;
    ```

    **3. Dynamic PIN based on date and time, with PAM style unlock enabled:**

    ```bash
    if [ "$AU_INPUT" = $(date +%m%H%M) ]; then exit 0; else exit 1; fi;
    ```

    **4. Uninstall apps:** (be extra careful, this is irreversible)

    ```bash
    for i in `pm list packages | grep -i -E 'torproject|mozilla.fenix|telegram' | cut -d : -f 2` ; do pm uninstall $i; done;
    ```

    **5. Wipe your device (sudo):** (Do not test this. You need to grant superuser to SystemUI in advance.)

    ```bash
    am broadcast -a android.intent.action.MASTER_CLEAR
    ```

    **6. Clear an app's data instead of uninstalling it:**

    ```bash
    for i in `pm list packages | grep -i -E 'telegram|twitter' | cut -d : -f 2` ; do pm clear $i; done;
    ```

    **7. Record the screen while the phone is being used (sudo):**

    ```bash
    (screenrecord --time-limit 180 /data/local/tmp/au.mp4 </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &)
    ```

    Recent Android versions restrict background `screenrecord`, test it on your device first.

    **8. Cut off and nuke ADB (sudo):**

    ```bash
    settings put global adb_enabled 0
    ADBD=$(readlink -f /proc/$(pgrep -x adbd)/exe)
    kill $(pgrep -x adbd)
    mount --bind /dev/null "$ADBD"
    ```

    The last three lines kill adbd and bind-mount `/dev/null` over its binary so init cannot restart it — this survives until you reboot. Since Android 11 adbd lives in an APEX, so `readlink` resolves the real path instead of hardcoding one. This only blocks adb; forensic tools bring their own.

    **9. Turn off root access for ADB, or entirely (sudo):**

    ```bash
    # 0 = Disabled, 1 = Apps only, 2 = ADB only, 3 = Apps and ADB (default)
    magisk --sqlite "UPDATE settings SET value=1 WHERE key='root_access'"
    ```

    `0` also revokes root from this module, so keep it at `1` if you only want to cut off adb. The `root_access` key exists in Magisk ≤ 31 and has been removed on master.

    **10. Delayed wipe — schedule it and walk away (sudo, dangerous):**

    ```bash
    (sleep 300; am broadcast -a android.intent.action.MASTER_CLEAR) &
    ```

    **11. Multiple fake passwords in one script (requires PAM style unlock):**

    ```bash
    case "$AU_INPUT" in
      # 1111: disable what you don't want to hand over, then unlock
      1111) for i in `pm list packages | grep -i -E 'telegram|twitter' | cut -d : -f 2` ; do pm disable $i; done
            exit 0 ;;

      # 2222: schedule a wipe 5 minutes out, and stay locked
      2222) (sleep 300; am broadcast -a android.intent.action.MASTER_CLEAR) &
            exit 1 ;;

      # 3333: unlock, but start recording what happens next
      3333) (screenrecord --time-limit 180 /data/local/tmp/au.mp4 </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &)
            exit 0 ;;

      # anything else: don't unlock
      *)    exit 1 ;;
    esac
    ```

    You can either bind this whole script to the module, or bind a different command to each fake password.

    Grab some of those or use your creativity to form a shell script yourself!
    
    \* You also need to make sure to put long tasks, such as web requests to background with '&' to prevent timeout.

    </details>
- Test your unlock by clicking "Restart SystemUI"

> [!NOTE]
> You may need to set mount namespace to system global namespace and disable mount namespace isolation in your superuser app (e.g., Magisk, APatch) for it to work on some devices.

> Pro tip: You can also use some automation software to make it easier to customize your commands ! just use a command like `am broadcast -a safety.intent.test` and catch the intent in your favorite app, it could be extended to do some stuff like take a picture, record audio, send an email, etc. like [Automate](https://llamalab.com/automate/) . Note this kind of software can't work before decryption, so just make it an addition to your commands separated with a `;`.

<details><summary>Here's how to use this module if you use <code>Pattern</code> for screen lock</summary>
  <ol>
  <li>Install and enable this module, open app and click 'Restart SystemUI'</li>
  <li>Grab logs with <code>adb logcat | grep alternativeUnlockHook</code> or your favorite log viewer (at <code>Debug</code> level)</li>
  <li>Unlock with your desired fake pattern</li>
  <li>Unlock with your real pattern</li>
  <li>You'll find two different <code>credStr</code> values from your unlocks in logcat; enter them into <code>fakePassword</code> and <code>realPassword</code></li>
  <li>Done! Now click 'Restart SystemUI' .<br>
  </ol>

## How does it work ?

When the fake password is provided, this module detects the input and replaces it with the real password. As a result, both the fake and real passwords can unlock the device, regardless of whether it is the first unlock or not.

Furthermore, since the fake password will be replaced with the real one, the fake password can also successfully decrypt the phone after a reboot.

## Contributing

This is a **security focused** app, at least for its usage. So before submitting your pull request, please note:

- Does this introduce any **security** weakness or **privacy** concern ?
- Is this **compatible** with existing installations, or does it **break** on some devices ? Does this use a feature that only present in some specific software/hardware environments ?
- We don't accept any **AI usage** for coding or documentation for **first-time contributors** . For existing contributors, please review every line of code and test it against a reasonable number of devices/AVDs. Please keep the code simple and maintainable :3
